svg.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Out-of-order core (Tomasulo + ROB): instruction flow
svg.text: Out-of-order core — the life of one instruction
Tomasulo + reorder buffer (32), single issue, 2 CDBs. Instructions enter and leave in program order (dispatch, commit); in between they wait, execute and finish in any order.
RAT → RF if still this tag
OUT OF ORDER — as soon as operands and a unit are ready
CDB broadcasts wake up waiting instructions (tag match, either bus)
commit frees the ROB entry → dispatch can continue · RAT entry back to the register file
mispredict found at execute: flush every younger entry (IQ, RS, LSQ, ROB), rebuild the RAT, fetch from the actual target
exception at the ROB head: flush everything, trap → mtvec (precise)
the reader holds the producer's ROB tag and waits in its RS until a CDB broadcasts that tag
gone: every result gets its own ROB entry (renaming), so a later write never touches an earlier reader's value
RS / LSQ / ROB full → dispatch stalls; 2 ALUs; MUL is pipelined; 2 CDBs → up to 2 results per cycle, oldest first
predicted at fetch (BHT + BTB); younger instructions run speculatively; a mispredict is flushed as soon as the branch executes
loads wait until all older store addresses are known; same address → take the store's data (forwarding); stores write at commit
marked in the ROB entry, taken only at the head → precise: older instructions done, younger never committed
load and MUL take 3 cycles; ALU 1 · 2 CDB broadcasts per cycle (oldest first) · a waiting instruction can issue the cycle after its value is broadcast
• #4 addi executes in cycle 6 and broadcasts in 7 — before the older #3 add (EX 7, WB 8), which waits for x4 from the load
• two CDBs: #2 mul and #4 addi broadcast in the same cycle (7), nobody waits for the bus
• commit stays in program order 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 — the register file only sees the program's order
• the store #6 writes memory at its commit (12), never speculatively
